Arithmetic and sutra naming are clean (96×119: dev −4/+19, cross-sum 115, dev-product −76, borrow 1 → 114|24 = 11424, matches; 82×89 → 72|98 = 7298, matches; complements are honest "all from 9, last from 10"). The failure is in the rule AS WRITTEN in the borrow case, where two of the three fields of step 5 still carry the positive-overflow text and contradict the arithmetic beside them.

second_example step 5: result = "the product −76 is negative, so complete it from the base: ceil(76/100)=1 => left 115−1 = 114, right 1×100−76 = 24" — correct trigger (negativity), correct direction (left DEcreases). But the same step's operation = "Adjust the right part to fit the base width" and description = "The right part cannot be wider than the base's zeros, so the excess moves into the left part — this carry is part of the method, not an afterthought" — byte-identical to the skeleton's positive-carry row.

Two concrete breaks:
1. Wrong trigger. −76 is two digits — exactly the base width. Nothing is "wider than the base's zeros", so the stated condition is false at the very moment the step fires. The rule as written does not survive the negative case; it only survives the 198 case in the skeleton. Per the near-base requirement, a negative product narrower than the base width still needs the borrow, and the taught condition here never fires on it.
2. Wrong direction, stated explicitly. "the excess moves into the left part" and the word "carry" describe an increase (skeleton: 71+1=72). The actual operation subtracts (115−1=114). A learner following the prose gets 116|24 = 11624, not 11424. The description does not merely under-specify the borrow — it asserts the opposite sign of adjustment.

This is a pattern-level, not row-level, defect: the grounding note records distinct step skeletons = 1 across all 29 rows, so every negative-deviation-product row in the group inherits the same width-framed operation label and increase-framed description over borrow arithmetic. The post-fix metrics cited ("rows never mentioning carry/borrow = 0", "Adjust step lacks explicit arithmetic = 0") are satisfied by the result field alone and do not detect that the surrounding rule text was never re-triggered for the sign case — the fix landed in the computation string only.

Grounding supports the correct form: Tirthaji_s0_00039 Note 2 scopes "keep the permissible two digits ... and carry the surplus" to the more-than-two-digit product case only, i.e. width overflow is the CARRY trigger, and says nothing that would justify applying that same sentence to a negative right part.

To pass, step 5 must branch its operation/description with the sign as the trigger — e.g. operation "Complete the negative right part from the base", description stating that a negative deviation product (of any width) is completed from the base and the borrowed multiple of the base is SUBTRACTED from the left part — while the skeleton's row keeps the width-overflow carry wording. common_mistakes[1] on second_example already names the correct behavior, which makes the contradiction inside the step itself more conspicuous, not less.

Both round-1/round-2 defects are fixed and verified by recomputation. Skeleton (82x89) genuinely exercises the carry: (-18)x(-11)=198 overflows the 2-digit base width, and step 5 shows the whole adjustment on-page — 198/100 = 1 r 98 => carry 1, new left 71+1=72, new right 98 — then step 6 assembles 72x100+98=7298 (true product 7298). Chaining is gap-free: step 3's 71 and step 4's 198 are step 5's only inputs; step 5's 72 and 98 are step 6's only inputs. second_example (96x119) shares the identical six-step skeleton with the same operation labels and holds under a different numeric configuration (mixed-sign deviations -4 and +19, so a borrow rather than a carry): cross-sum 96+19=115 (cross-checks as 119-4=115), (-4)(+19)=-76, and the adjust step states and computes the borrow-size rule in view — ceil(76/100)=1 => left 115-1=114, right 1x100-76=24 — assembling to 114x100+24=11424 (true product 11424). No figure in either adjust step arrives from off-page. Non-blocking nit for the generator: step 5's `description` is shared boilerplate written only for the overflow direction ("the excess moves into the left part"), so in the borrow instance it sits beside arithmetic that reduces the left part by 1; the `result` line and common_mistakes both state the borrow correctly, so the learner is not stranded, but the description contradicts its own step. Likewise step 4's "The right part occupies 2 digits" prints against 198 and -76 — acceptable only because step 5 now actually resolves it. Recommend making step 5's description case-dependent (carry vs. complete-from-base) on the next pass.

Both rows' traps are exercised by their own numerics, and the two rows carry DIFFERENT, config-tailored mistake lists rather than shared boilerplate. Skeleton 82x89: deviations -18 and -11 are both negative, so the "two minuses give a positive right part" trap is live; (-18)(-11)=198 genuinely exceeds the 2-digit base width, so the overflow/carry trap is live and step 5 shows 71+1=72 | 98. Second example 96x119: deviations -4 and +19 are genuinely mixed-sign, so the "sign error with one positive one negative deviation" trap is live; the right part (-76) is genuinely negative, so the "complete from base and reduce the left part by the borrow" trap is live and step 5 shows 115-1=114 | 24. No trap references a hazard the configuration does not contain, and no row is missing the trap its numerics do create. Arithmetic verified independently: 82-11=89-18=71, 71*100+198=7298; 96+19=119-4=115, 115*100-76=11424=96*119. Scaffold place_value_chart matches the manipulation, since the whole hazard surface is the right part being exactly as wide as the base's zeros, with carry and borrow crossing that width boundary. expected_time 85s is plausible (mildly generous) for a 6-step L3 near-base product with a carry/borrow adjustment. Only nit, not disqualifying: 119's deviation of +19 is a stretch for the literal "all from 9, last from 10" complement framing, but the grounding (Tirthaji_s0_00039, Bhatia_s0_00043) covers above-base operands and the cross-sum still resolves identically, so the method is applied correctly.

Wrong-trigger rule survives only the positive case. Arithmetic is clean in both rows (844x952=803488, 1007x980=986860; both cross-sums agree at 796 and 987 respectively), but the invariant step-5 description — byte-identical in skeleton and second_example — states exactly one trigger: "The right part cannot be wider than the base's zeros, so the excess moves into the left part — this carry is part of the method, not an afterthought". In second_example the deviation product is -140, whose magnitude is 3 digits = exactly the base-1000 width, i.e. NOT wider than the base's zeros and carrying no "excess" — yet a borrow is still mandatory. Applying the rule as written to -140 yields "it already fits, no adjustment", assembling 987|140 = 987140 instead of 986860. This is precisely the negative-product-narrower-than-base-width case the trigger must cover, and the stated rule fails it. The step's operation label repeats the same defect ("Adjust the right part to fit the base width"), and the description calls the move a "carry" when second_example actually decrements the left part (987-1=986), a borrow. The correct trigger is stated ONLY inside that single row's result string ("the product -140 is negative, so complete it from the base"), i.e. as a per-instance observation, never as the pattern-level rule that generalizes to the other 29 rows; the grounding_note's own verification metric ("rows whose Adjust step lacks explicit arithmetic = 0") measures presence of arithmetic, not correctness of the stated condition, so it does not catch this. Secondary (non-decisive): sub_category is named "Nikhilam Navatashcaramam (All from 9, Last from 10)" but the complement procedure the sutra names is never taught — step 2 in both rows defines deviations only as "Deviation = number - base", while Tirthaji_s0_00039 states the naming rule verbatim ("all the other digits ... are to be subtracted from 9 but the last ... should be deducted from 10"). Fix: split the adjust step's rule into both branches — negative deviation product => complete from the base and reduce the left part by ceil(|p|/base); non-negative product wider than the base's zeros => keep the low digits and carry the surplus left — so the rule text itself, not just one result line, covers both.

Both prior failures are repaired and verified by recomputation. Skeleton (844x952) genuinely exercises the carry: step 5 shows 7488 / 1000 = 7 r 488, carry 7, left 796 + 7 = 803, right 488, assembling to 803488 (= true product). Second example (1007x980) exercises the mirror case with visible sizing arithmetic: ceil(140/1000) = 1, left 987 - 1 = 986, right 1x1000 - 140 = 860, assembling to 986860 (= true product); no figure in the adjust step is asserted off-page, and the ceil rule generalizes correctly (e.g. -1400 -> borrow 2, right 600). Step N output feeds step N+1 with no gaps in both: 796 and 7488/-140 enter step 5; 803/488 and 986/860 exit into step 6. The two instances share one six-step skeleton and differ only in numeric configuration, so the adjust slot holds under both an over-wide positive right part and a negative one. Remaining defect, not blocking: step 5's description is un-parameterized boilerplate — in the second example it reads "the excess moves into the left part — this carry is part of the method" while the result line performs a borrow that reduces the left part (987 - 1 = 986), so the prose contradicts the direction of the arithmetic on the very step that failed in rounds 1 and 2. The result line is self-contained and correct and the operation label ("Adjust the right part to fit the base width") fits both cases, so a learner can still follow the chain, but the description must be branched carry-vs-borrow. Secondary nit: step 3 asserts "either cross-sum gives the same left part" while showing only one of the two (844 - 48 = 796; 952 - 156 is not displayed).

Trap-realism check passes on both examples; each row's common_mistakes name hazards that its own numeric configuration actually creates.

Skeleton (844 × 952, base 1000): deviations are -156 and -48 — both negative, so mistake #1 ("treating the product of two negative deviations as negative") is a live hazard, and the shown right-part product (-156)(-48)=7488 genuinely exceeds the 3-digit base width, so mistake #2 (overflow not carried) is exercised by the displayed arithmetic, not just asserted. Math verified: cross-sum 844-48 = 952-156 = 796; 7488 -> carry 7, left 803, right 488; 803488 = 844×952. ✓

Second example (1007 × 980, base 1000): deviations +7 and -20 — genuinely mixed sign, so mistake #1 ("sign error when one deviation is positive and the other negative") is exercised; the right part 7×(-20) = -140 is genuinely negative, so mistake #2 (failing to complete from the base and reduce the left part) is exercised. Math verified: cross-sum 1007-20 = 980+7 = 987; borrow 1 -> left 986, right 1000-140 = 860; 986860 = 1007×980. ✓

Notably the two rows carry DIFFERENT mistake lists matched to their own sign configuration (both-negative/overflow vs. mixed-sign/borrow) rather than a copied generic list — that is the failure mode this lens hunts for, and it is absent. Traps are grounded in the corpus: Tirthaji_s0_00039 states the carry rule for an over-wide right part; Bhatia_s0_00047 covers the above/below-base (negative RHS) completion.

Scaffold place_value_chart matches the manipulation — the method's core act is placing a right part of exactly base-zero width and moving surplus/borrow across the column boundary, which is a place-value operation. expected_time 120s is plausible for L4 3-digit near-base work that includes a carry (844: deviation 156 requires a nontrivial 156×48) or a borrow.

Minor, non-blocking: step 4's description ("The right part occupies 3 digits") sits above a result that is 7488 / -140 and therefore does NOT yet occupy 3 digits — the reconciliation only arrives in step 5. The description reads as slightly premature but is not wrong as a statement of the width rule, and step 5 supplies explicit arithmetic in both rows. Not grounds for refutation.

What is fixed: the carry step now survives. Step 4 in both rows shows explicit arithmetic (1600 ÷ 1000 = 1 r 600 → carry 1, left 920+1=921; 43264 ÷ 1000 = 43 r 264 → carry 43, left 1416+43=1459), the trigger stated is width overflow of the squared deviation, which is the correct trigger here — and because the right part in Yavadunam squaring is (deviation)², it is never negative, so the borrow branch genuinely cannot arise and its absence is not a gap. Both answers are right (960²=921600, 1208²=1459264) and both match the Tirthaji verbatim pattern (1039²=10781/521=1079/521, 965²=9301/225=931/225).

What still refutes it — step 2 states the rule with the wrong direction for the surplus case. The description is the same frozen string in both rows: "Whatever the deficiency, lessen it further." In second_example the deviation is +208 and the step actually computes 1208+208 = 1416, i.e. it INCREASES. The learner is handed a rule that says lessen while the worked line adds. The sub_category itself advertises "Deficiency/Surplus Squaring," so the surplus branch is in scope and the grounding supplies only the deficiency half of the sutra (Bhatia: "whatever the extent of its deficiency, lessen it to the same extent"); Tirthaji's surplus examples (113²=1261/69, 1007²=1014/049, 10017²) are the corollary form — "whatever the surplus, increase it further by that much" — and that half is never stated. The rule as written does not survive both signs, which is exactly the trigger-correctness bar. The operation label ("add the deviation again") is sign-general and fine; the description under it is not, and it is the description that carries the sutra.

Secondary, same root cause (sign/width-blind template text): step 3's description asserts "The right part occupies 3 digits — the width of the base's zeros" while displaying 1600 (4 digits) and 43264 (5 digits) as that right part. Step 4 later resolves it, but as written step 3 is a false statement sitting directly above its own contradicting result.

Since the grounding_note reports distinct step skeletons = 1 across all 24 rows, this wording defect is group-wide, not a one-row slip: every surplus-deviation row in the group tells the student to lessen while adding. Fix is narrow — condition the step-2 description on the sign of the deviation (deficiency → "lessen it further by the same amount"; surplus → "increase it further by the same amount"), and reword step 3 to say the right part is written into a 3-digit slot rather than that it occupies 3 digits.

Both prior failure modes are demonstrably fixed and every figure verifies. Skeleton (960^2, base 1000): -40 -> left 920 -> (-40)^2=1600 -> step 4 shows "1600 div 1000 = 1 r 600 => carry 1, left 920+1=921, right 600" -> 921|600 = 921600 (correct). The width rule asserted in step 3 ("right part occupies 3 digits — the width of the base's zeros") is no longer asserted-then-silently-violated: 1600 is 4 digits and step 4 discharges the excess on-page, with divisor (= the base named in the problem statement), quotient, remainder, new left and new right all computed in view. No off-page arithmetic anywhere; step N's output is step N+1's stated input with no gaps (S1 -40 -> S2; S2 920 + S3 1600 -> S4; S4 921/600 -> S5). second_example (1208^2, base 1000) is the same 5-step skeleton with identical operation labels, and the adjust step holds under a genuinely different configuration — surplus rather than deficiency, and a two-digit carry: 208^2 = 43264, 43264 div 1000 = 43 r 264, left 1416+43 = 1459, right 264, 1459|264 = 1459264 = 1208^2 (verified). Carry/borrow is exercised in both, so the level teaches what it exists to teach.

Two non-blocking defects worth passing to the generator. (1) Step 2's description string "Whatever the deficiency, lessen it further" is shared verbatim across the skeleton and is wrong-signed for surplus instances: in second_example it sits above "1208+208 = 1416", so a learner reading the prose rather than the result line would subtract 208 and get 1000. Only the description is wrong — the operation label ("Left part: add the deviation again") and the explicit result arithmetic are both correct, so the misdirection is self-correcting within the same line, which is why this is not a fail. Fix by branching the description on deviation sign ("whatever the surplus, increase it further"). (2) common_mistakes flags "right part written with too few digits (missing leading zeros)", but neither instance produces a remainder needing a leading zero (600, 264 are both already 3 wide), so that mistake is named without ever being demonstrated; a padding instance in the group would close it. Neither issue touches the carry demonstration, the on-page adjust arithmetic, or step-to-step continuity.

Packet: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-harshahirrao-Speed-gym/9e5da183-7e68-48e6-be30-660db64bf5ce/scratchpad/stage7_r2/target_3.json (squaring / Yavadunam L4). Both common_mistakes are hazards this configuration does not exercise, and neither names the hazard the configuration actually creates.

(1) "right part written with too few digits (missing leading zeros)" — this trap requires deviation^2 to be NARROWER than the base's zero-width. In both shown examples the opposite holds: 960 → (-40)^2 = 1600 (4 digits vs base width 3), 1208 → (+208)^2 = 43264 (5 digits vs 3). After the step-4 adjustment the right parts are 600 and 264 — both already exactly 3 digits, so no leading zero is ever needed and a student literally cannot commit this error here. The grounding_note itself concedes the L4 design ("the squared deviation is usually wider than the base width at L4, so the excess carries left"; "rows whose solution never mentions a carry/borrow = 0" across all 24), which means the padding trap is structurally excluded from the whole group, not just these two rows.

(2) "squaring the deviation but dropping its sign context" — squaring is sign-annihilating by definition: (-40)^2 and (+40)^2 are both 1600, and the right part is positive in every row. There is no step in either example where the sign of the squared deviation changes the answer, so the stated mistake is vacuous as written. The genuine sign hazard at this target lives one step earlier (left part = N + d, i.e. 960-40=920 for the deficit vs 1208+208=1416 for the surplus), and the mistake text explicitly anchors on the squaring step instead, so it does not cover it. The mixed-sign pairing of the two examples is real but goes untrapped.

Uncovered real hazard: the carry from the over-wide squared deviation into the left part (1600 → carry 1, 920+1=921; 43264 → carry 43, 1416+43=1459). This is the one error every row of the group can produce — dropping the carry, or carrying the wrong magnitude (carrying 4 instead of 43 for a two-digit carry) — and it appears in no common_mistake. Fix: replace mistake (2) with the carry-drop/carry-magnitude error and re-point mistake (1) at the left-part direction error under a negative deviation (adding 40 instead of subtracting), or re-configure some group rows with small deviations (e.g. 1007, 996) so the leading-zero trap is genuinely reachable.

Non-blocking: visual_scaffold place_value_chart is an acceptable match for the width/carry placement manipulation, and expected_time 115s is plausible for a 3-digit-deviation square (208^2 = 43264) plus carry assembly. The failure is trap realism only.
